newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian oil reserves 30-50 mln tonnes - report.
newsitem.headline: Latvian oil reserves 30-50 mln tonnes - report.

text.p: Oil reserves on Latvia's continental shelf and onshore are 30 to 50 million tonnes and could be worth $15 billion at prices expected in the world market next century, a report quoted in newspaper Diena said on Friday.

The newspaper quoted research by the Latvian Energy Agency which gave the figures after seismic research started in the 1980s. The forecasts are part of a project to explore and exploit oil and create a local oil industry.
The plan, ordererd by the economy ministry in summer of 1996, will now be looked at by the government.

A foreign company or group of companies ready to assume the financial risk would be granted the right to prospect for oil as the total estimated cost would be around eight billion dollars, the newspaper quoted the report as adding.

Western companies have already said they want to prospect for oil in Latvian territorial waters but a deal with Amoco and Swedish Olje Prospektering has been delayed by a sea border dispute with Lithuania.
The document also said that a national oil company should be formed to protect the commercial interests of Latvia.
